description: This topic explains what a system and an information system are, the role of a system analyst, and the stages of the System Development Life Cycle used to study, design, build, implement, and maintain computer-based systems.

options.text: A single computer program used by one person
A collection of related parts that work together to achieve a common goal
A type of computer hardware only
A list of instructions stored on a disk

mcq.explanation: A system is a set of related components that interact and work together to achieve a particular objective.

mcq.questionText: Which best describes an information system?

options.text: A system that collects, processes, stores, and distributes information
A system made only of cables and wires
A printer connected to a computer
A folder of paper documents in an office

mcq.explanation: An information system gathers data, processes it into information, stores it, and distributes it to users to support decision making.

options.text: Building the hardware of a computer
The study of an existing system to find out how it works and how it can be improved

mcq.explanation: System analysis is the detailed study of a current system to understand its operation, problems, and requirements for improvement.

mcq.questionText: Who is responsible for studying and designing information systems in an organisation?
mcq.explanation: A system analyst investigates user needs, analyses the existing system, and designs a new or improved system.

mcq.questionText: What does the abbreviation SDLC stand for?
mcq.explanation: SDLC stands for System Development Life Cycle, the set of stages followed when developing an information system.

mcq.questionText: Which stage of the SDLC usually comes first?
mcq.explanation: Development begins with identifying the problem or carrying out a preliminary study before any other work is done.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of a feasibility study?

options.text: To decide whether the proposed system is worth developing
To train the users of the system
To repair faults after the system is in use

mcq.explanation: A feasibility study checks whether the proposed system is practical and worthwhile in terms of technical, economic, and operational factors.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a fact-finding method used during requirements analysis?
mcq.explanation: Interviews are a common fact-finding method where the analyst asks users questions to gather requirements.

mcq.questionText: A questionnaire is most useful when the analyst needs to:

options.text: Collect information from many people quickly
Watch how a single worker performs a task

mcq.explanation: A questionnaire uses a set of written questions and is efficient for gathering responses from a large number of people.

mcq.questionText: During which changeover method does the old and new system run at the same time?
mcq.explanation: In parallel changeover both the old and new systems operate together for a period so results can be compared before the old one is dropped.

mcq.questionText: What is the main aim of testing a system before it is used?

options.text: To find and remove errors so the system works correctly
To increase the price of the system
To draw the data flow diagrams

mcq.explanation: Testing checks the system against requirements to detect and correct errors before it goes into real use.

mcq.questionText: Which type of documentation is written mainly for the people who will operate the system?
mcq.explanation: User documentation, such as a user manual, explains how to use the system in simple language for ordinary users.

mcq.questionText: Economic feasibility is mainly concerned with:

options.text: Whether the right technology is available
Whether the benefits of the system are worth its costs
Whether users will accept the system
Whether the colours of the screen are attractive

mcq.explanation: Economic feasibility compares the costs of developing and running the system with the expected financial benefits.

mcq.questionText: What happens during the maintenance stage of the SDLC?

options.text: The system is studied for the first time
The system is corrected, updated, and improved while in use
The feasibility study is carried out

mcq.explanation: Maintenance keeps the working system running well by fixing faults and making improvements after implementation.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common reason why a new system may fail?

options.text: Poor planning and inadequate user requirements

mcq.explanation: Systems often fail because of poor planning, unclear requirements, lack of user involvement, or insufficient testing and training.

fib.questionText: A _____ is a set of related parts that work together to achieve a common goal.
fib.explanation: A system is made up of related components that interact to reach a shared objective.

fib.questionText: An information system collects data and processes it into useful _____ for users.
fib.explanation: An information system turns raw data into meaningful information used for decision making.

fib.questionText: The person who studies and designs information systems is called a system _____.
fib.explanation: The system analyst investigates needs and designs the new or improved system.

fib.questionText: The abbreviation SDLC stands for System Development Life _____.
fib.explanation: SDLC means System Development Life Cycle, the stages used to build a system.

fib.questionText: A _____ study is carried out to decide whether a proposed system is worth developing.
fib.explanation: The feasibility study examines whether the system is technically, economically, and operationally practical.

fib.questionText: Watching how workers perform their tasks to gather facts is a method called _____.
fib.explanation: Observation is a fact-finding method where the analyst watches activities directly.

fib.questionText: In _____ changeover, the old system is completely replaced by the new one at once.
fib.explanation: Direct changeover stops the old system and starts the new one immediately, which is risky if errors occur.

fib.questionText: Trying out a new system in one branch or department before using it everywhere is called _____ changeover.
fib.explanation: Pilot changeover introduces the new system in one part of the organisation first to reduce risk.

fib.questionText: Documentation that explains how the system was built, for programmers and analysts, is called _____ documentation.
fib.explanation: Technical documentation describes the design and code so it can be maintained by technical staff.

fib.questionText: Fixing errors and making improvements to a system after it is in use is known as system _____.
fib.explanation: Maintenance keeps the live system working correctly and up to date.

tf.questionText: A system is made up of related parts that work together towards a common goal.
tf.explanation: This is the correct definition of a system.

tf.questionText: An information system only stores data and never processes it.
tf.explanation: An information system collects, processes, stores, and distributes information; processing is a key part.

tf.questionText: System analysis involves studying an existing system to understand and improve it.
tf.explanation: Analysis is the detailed study of how a current system works and how it can be improved.

tf.questionText: A system analyst mainly repairs broken computer hardware.
tf.explanation: A system analyst studies needs and designs systems; hardware repair is done by technicians.

tf.questionText: The feasibility study is done to decide whether a proposed system should be developed.
tf.explanation: The feasibility study checks if the system is worthwhile before development continues.

tf.questionText: Interviews, questionnaires, observation, and document review are all fact-finding methods.
tf.explanation: These are the main methods used to gather facts during requirements analysis.

tf.questionText: In parallel changeover the old system is switched off before the new system starts.
tf.explanation: In parallel changeover both systems run together for a time; that statement describes direct changeover.

tf.questionText: Testing is done to find and remove errors before the system is put into use.
tf.explanation: Testing checks the system against requirements to detect and correct errors.

tf.questionText: User documentation is written in technical language for programmers only.
tf.explanation: User documentation is written in simple language for ordinary users; technical documentation is for programmers.

tf.questionText: Operational feasibility considers whether the users and the organisation will accept and use the system.
tf.explanation: Operational feasibility checks how well the system will fit into and be accepted by the organisation.

summary.questionText: Define a system in one sentence.
summary.correctAnswer: A system is a collection of related parts that work together to achieve a common goal.
summary.explanation: A system has interacting components and a shared objective.

summary.correctAnswer: An information system is a system that collects, processes, stores, and distributes information to support decision making.
summary.explanation: It turns data into useful information for its users.

summary.questionText: State the role of a system analyst.
summary.correctAnswer: A system analyst studies the existing system, gathers user requirements, and designs a new or improved system.
summary.explanation: The analyst bridges user needs and the technical solution.

summary.questionText: List the main stages of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
summary.correctAnswer: Problem identification, feasibility study, requirements analysis, system design, coding, testing, implementation, and maintenance.
summary.explanation: These ordered stages guide the development of an information system.

summary.questionText: Name the three types of feasibility studied before developing a system.
summary.correctAnswer: Technical feasibility, economic feasibility, and operational feasibility.
summary.explanation: These check whether the system is possible, affordable, and acceptable.

summary.questionText: List four fact-finding methods used during requirements analysis.
summary.correctAnswer: Interviews, questionnaires, observation, and document review.
summary.explanation: These methods help the analyst gather accurate information about user needs.

summary.questionText: Name the four common system changeover methods.
summary.correctAnswer: Direct, parallel, phased, and pilot changeover.
summary.explanation: Each method differs in how the new system replaces the old one.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between user documentation and technical documentation.
summary.correctAnswer: User documentation explains how to use the system in simple language for users, while technical documentation describes the design and code for programmers and analysts.
summary.explanation: They target different audiences and purposes.

summary.questionText: Why is system maintenance important after implementation?
summary.correctAnswer: Maintenance corrects errors, updates the system, and makes improvements so it keeps working well and meeting user needs.
summary.explanation: Systems must adapt to faults and changing requirements over time.

summary.questionText: Give two reasons why a new system may fail.
summary.correctAnswer: Poor planning or unclear requirements, and lack of user involvement or inadequate testing and training.
summary.explanation: Failures often come from weak analysis, planning, and preparation of users.

hoq.questionText: A school wants to replace its manual student records with a new computer system but is worried about losing important data if the new system has hidden errors. Which changeover method is the safest choice and why?

options.text: Direct changeover, because it is the fastest
Parallel changeover, because the old system keeps running so results can be compared and used as backup
Phased changeover, because only screens are changed
No changeover is needed, the old system can simply be deleted

hoq.explanation: Parallel changeover runs both systems together, so if the new system fails the old one is still available, protecting the data.

hoq.questionText: An analyst must gather detailed opinions from a few senior managers and also collect quick answers from hundreds of junior staff. Which combination of fact-finding methods is most suitable?

options.text: Interviews for the managers and questionnaires for the junior staff
Questionnaires for the managers and interviews for all junior staff
Document review only, with no contact with people

hoq.explanation: Interviews give deep responses from a few people, while questionnaires efficiently collect answers from large numbers, so the combination fits both needs.

hoq.questionText: A company has the money and skilled staff for a new system, and the technology exists, but most workers refuse to use it and prefer the old way. Which feasibility was most likely overlooked?
hoq.explanation: Operational feasibility checks whether users will accept and use the system; here the technology and money were fine but user acceptance was not considered.
